title: Customer Insights - Journeys: Journey Creation Agent builds journeys from a plain-language description
summary: The briefing passes: its enablement requirements, licensing, roles and automation are supported, and its rollout facts match the roadmap. Minor corrections should extend the credit-allocation path to the tenant-capacity checkbox and name the API request-body properties that control allocation and overages.

claims.claim: Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits > environment > Allocate capacity reaches credit allocation and the panel containing tenant-capacity overage control.
claims.quote: Under Allocate capacity, enter the number of Copilot Credits to allocate to the environment. Under Capacity overages, select or clear Draw from the available capacity in my tenant to control what happens when the environment exhausts its allocation.
claims.fix: Keep the allocation path, and append in controls[2].note: 'In the same panel, under Capacity overages, select or clear Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.' This completes the route to the second control named by the row.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table and closing automation sentence
claims.claim: PUT /licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 writes an environment's Copilot Credit allocation and tenant-capacity enforcement rule.
claims.quote: All programmatic examples in this article use API version 2024-10-01. Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion"
claims.fix: Keep the call. Add to controls[2].note: 'The request body identifies scope.environmentId and sets allocatedEntitlements[].entitlementId to MCSMessages, allocation.quantity to the allocated credits, and enforcementRules[].ruleType to TenantPool with enabled controlling tenant-capacity draw.'
